name: Arkansas
nameStory: French traders' spelling of an Illinois-language word for the Quapaw, 'akansa' - the downstream people. Arkansas and Kansas share that root, but Arkansas kept the silent French 's.' The pronunciation fight got so heated the legislature passed a law in 1881 declaring it 'AR-kan-saw.'
capitalStory: French explorers coming up the Arkansas River crossed miles of flat delta mud, then hit a small stone outcrop - 'la Petite Roche,' the little rock. It was the first solid landmark telling you the flatland was over and the highlands had begun.

majorFeatures.name: Arkansas River
majorFeatures.note: Cuts the state in half diagonally

funFacts: Crater of Diamonds is the only public diamond mine in the world where you keep whatever you dig up.
Hot Springs was federally protected in 1832, forty years before Yellowstone.
Walmart, the world's largest company by revenue, is headquartered in Bentonville.
The Ouachitas run east-west, which is unusual; most North American ranges run north-south.
whyItMatters: In 1957 the Little Rock Nine were blocked from Central High until President Eisenhower sent the 101st Airborne to escort them - the first time since Reconstruction that federal troops enforced Black civil rights in the South.
